indicators.note: backing means the phrase found for the TV-show words is read from back to front

parts.note: a show by one performer is a solo gig

explanation.surface: Paid companions are seen supporting a BBC evening magazine programme.
explanation.walkthrough: The One Show is a BBC early-evening TV programme, but here it is read literally as a one-person show, a SOLO GIG; 'backing' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Men paid to accompany women are hired male companions, the same idea as plural escorts.

indicators.note: Sounds says the word for good is to be heard, then spelt as the rock name

parts.note: good means nice

explanation.surface: A reply approving the suggestion of a rock.
explanation.walkthrough: 14 is ROCK AND ROLL, so '14 (part 1)' means rock; gneiss, a banded metamorphic rock, is said like 'nice'.
explanation.definitionFit: Gneiss is a coarse banded metamorphic stone, an example of the geological kind of rock.

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the pieces are read from the bottom upwards, so backwards

parts.note: an orb is a circle or ring
a bag is a carrier, as in carrier bag

explanation.surface: A ring-bearer rising to the occasion for rock music.
explanation.walkthrough: '14 (part 1)' is ROCK, from 14's ROCK AND ROLL; ORB and BAG are both turned by 'up', giving the dark igneous rock.
explanation.definitionFit: Gabbro is a dark coarse-grained igneous stone, an example of geological rock.

indicators.note: producing suggests the letters of the preceding words are worked into something new

explanation.surface: A sluggish journey leaves the traveller feeling down.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling gloomy and dejected is a state of mental depression, the plural phrase used as a mood.

indicators.note: enter says one piece goes into another

parts.note: sole means only, as in sole survivor
V is the Roman numeral for five

explanation.surface: An instruction that just five people may come in and reply.
explanation.definitionFit: To answer a puzzle is to work it out, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Run into daughter taking dog outside

indicators.note: outside says the dog word sits around the daughter letter

parts.note: a collie is a breed of dog

explanation.surface: Someone bumps into their daughter as she takes the dog out for a walk.
explanation.definitionFit: To crash into something is to strike it, a verb synonym of run into.

indicators.note: ordered means the letters are put in a new order

parts.note: the figure 1 looks like the letter I
NT is the New Testament, a set of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: Looks like a cross-reference to 1 across with a request for books.
explanation.walkthrough: '1 across' looks like a cross-reference but is read literally: I plus ACROSS is rearranged, then NT added. '14 (part 2)' is ROLL from ROCK AND ROLL.
explanation.definitionFit: A croissant is a crescent-shaped bread item, an example of a breakfast roll.

indicators.note: before puts the left letter ahead of the winner's

parts.note: the winner comes 1ST, the figure 1 read as I

explanation.surface: The victor departed ahead of the music.
explanation.definitionFit: A roll is a register of names, as in a roll call, which is a catalogue of entries.

clue.text: Trendy suit results in lack of mobility

parts.note: in means fashionable or trendy
a suit is a legal action

explanation.surface: Wearing a fashionable outfit makes it hard to move.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing nothing, staying still, is idleness: a lack of mobility.

indicators.note: in a down clue beneath puts the fishing word under the medical letters

parts.note: ENT is ear, nose and throat, the hospital department dealing with those passages
to angle is to fish

explanation.surface: A fish gets caught up under hospital tubing.
explanation.definitionFit: To tangle or snarl things up is to twist them together.

indicators.note: movement says the letters of the preceding word are moved about

explanation.surface: An earthy instruction about the digestive system.
explanation.definitionFit: To shove someone aside with your arm is to push them out of the way.

clue.text: Elegant peer first to shake a leg

indicators.note: first says the peering word comes ahead of the elegant one

parts.note: to peer is to look
smart means elegant

explanation.surface: A stylish nobleman is asked to dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Peer' tempts as a nobleman; it is the verb, to look.
explanation.definitionFit: 'Look smart!' and 'shake a leg' are both idioms urging someone to hurry up.

indicators.note: foreign suggests the word's letters are made strange, rearranged

explanation.surface: A tempting display of wall-hangings from abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: A burlesque act of slowly undressing is a teasing display, hence a tantalising exhibition.

indicators.note: Over means the word for heads is turned round

parts.note: nut is slang for a head

explanation.surface: Overhead costs of a rock band, it seems.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Overheads' must be split into 'Over' and 'heads'. '14 (part 1)' is ROCK, here the verb: to shock.
explanation.definitionFit: To rock someone is to shock or daze them, which is to stun.

indicators.note: out signals the letters are put out of order

explanation.surface: A request to dispatch the senior nurse to fetch the decorations.
explanation.definitionFit: Ornaments that beautify are trimmings or decorations, a plural synonym.

clue.text: Sticky sweet with a new, amusing "pop"?

parts.note: rock is a hard stick-shaped seaside sweet
droll means amusing

explanation.surface: A candy described as a funny new soft drink.
explanation.walkthrough: Seaside rock is a British sugary stick sold at the coast. 'Pop' looks like a fizzy drink but means popular music.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1950s style of popular music is an example of pop, hence the question mark.

explanation.surface: A typist's instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: A person of a certain sort is a type; a single written symbol is a letter.

indicators.note: turned over means the whole run of pieces is read backwards

parts.note: a rack is a framework for holding things
cots are small beds

explanation.surface: A racing driver flipped over the bed frames.
explanation.definitionFit: A modified saloon used in banger-style track races is a kind of racer.

clue.text: Play a tambour by holy shrine

indicators.note: Play suggests the letters are played about with

explanation.surface: Someone drums beside a sacred site.
explanation.definitionFit: In North Africa the tomb of a Muslim holy man is a shrine with this name.

clue.text: He solicits cheers when guinea pig hides oven mitt at first

indicators.note: hides says the tester word conceals the other pieces

parts.note: a guinea pig is a tester, a taster of food
an oast is a kiln, an oven for drying hops

indicators.note: at first means only the first letter of the following word is taken

explanation.surface: A food tester concealing an oven glove.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Guinea pig' looks like the pet but means a test subject; 'cheers' means toasts.
explanation.definitionFit: The master of ceremonies at a banquet calls on guests to raise glasses, soliciting cheers.

clue.text: Invented language for the king of 14, when drunk

indicators.note: when drunk means the name is slurred, its final s becoming sh

parts.note: Elvis Presley was the King of Rock and Roll

explanation.surface: A slurred tribute to the King.
explanation.walkthrough: A drunk slurs 's' as 'sh', so ELVIS becomes the Tolkien tongue.
explanation.definitionFit: Tolkien constructed the tongues of his elves, an artificial or invented language.

indicators.note: takes means the snake word holds the shelter word inside

parts.note: an asp is a snake
lee is shelter from wind

explanation.surface: A snake hides away for its winter sleep.
explanation.definitionFit: An animal in winter dormancy is sleeping, so hibernating is a sleeping state.

indicators.note: heart extracted from means the middle letter of the colour word is removed

parts.note: coral is a pinkish colour

explanation.surface: A pink centre is mined out of a stone.
explanation.definitionFit: Coal is a sedimentary combustible stone, an example of rock.

clue.text: Copies many expressions introduced by footballers

indicators.note: introduced by puts the football letters at the front

parts.note: FA is the Football Association
C is the Roman numeral for 100, many
similes are figures of speech, expressions

explanation.surface: Footballers bring in lots of catchphrases that others repeat.
explanation.definitionFit: Exact reproductions of documents are replicas or copies.

explanation.surface: Directing someone on a cattle farm.
explanation.definitionFit: To guide is to direct a course; a young castrated bull raised on a ranch is the animal.

parts.note: the second part of 14 is roll, and a bun is a bread roll

explanation.surface: A baseball stroke arrives right on cue.
explanation.walkthrough: In baseball, a bunt is a soft hit made by tapping the ball with a loosely held bat.
explanation.definitionFit: A gentle tap with the bat in baseball is a particular kind of hit.

indicators.note: seizes means the flirt word grips the recipe letter

parts.note: a coquette is a flirt
R is the abbreviation for recipe, from Latin

explanation.surface: A flirtatious woman snatches a cooking recipe.
explanation.definitionFit: A crumbed fried cylinder of mashed potato or meat is a fried roll.

clue.text: Sound hooter when one goes in

indicators.note: goes in means the one letter is placed inside the hooter word

parts.note: hooter is slang for the nose
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A car horn sounds when someone climbs in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hooter' suggests a horn; it is slang for a nose.
explanation.definitionFit: Any audible din or racket is a sound.

clue.text: 14 (part 2) on tip of tendon or muscle

parts.note: the second part of 14 is roll, and a rota is a roll or roster of duties

indicators.note: tip of means the first letter of the following word

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Rolling about on a tendon or muscle injury.
explanation.definitionFit: A rotator is a muscle that turns a limb, as in the shoulder's rotator cuff.

parts.note: rosé is a pink wine
hip means fashionable, with it

explanation.surface: A suggestion to drink wine with dessert.
explanation.definitionFit: The red seed pod of a rose bush is a berry-like fruit.
